# Calendar App Dark Theme Color Palettes

Covers how Google Calendar, Apple Calendar, Outlook, and Fantastical handle
event category colors in dark mode. See [citations.md](../citations.md) for
source details.

## Google Calendar

### Light Mode Event Colors (API Values)

Google Calendar defines 11 event colors with dark text (#1d1d1d) foreground [4]:

| ID | Name | Hex | Description |
|----|------|-----|-------------|
| 1 | Lavender | #a4bdfc | Light periwinkle |
| 2 | Sage | #7ae7bf | Mint green |
| 3 | Grape | #dbadff | Light purple |
| 4 | Flamingo | #ff887c | Salmon pink |
| 5 | Banana | #fbd75b | Warm yellow |
| 6 | Tangerine | #ffb878 | Light orange |
| 7 | Peacock | #46d6db | Teal cyan |
| 8 | Graphite | #e1e1e1 | Light gray |
| 9 | Blueberry | #5484ed | Medium blue |
| 10 | Basil | #51b749 | Green |
| 11 | Tomato | #dc2127 | Red |

Additionally, 24 calendar-level colors are defined [4] ranging from Cocoa
(#ac725e) to Amethyst (#a47ae2).

### Dark Mode Adaptation

Google Calendar added web dark mode in October 2024 with Material Design 3 [3].
The team created "an internal system for adapting a wide range of colors to dark
theme" by "desaturating hues and defining brightness, while still letting users
express themselves in any shade of the rainbow" [3].

The exact dark-mode hex values are **not publicly documented** [3]. The API
returns only light-mode values [4]. The adaptation uses algorithmic
transformation rather than a fixed dark palette, but the specific desaturation
percentages and brightness adjustments are internal to Google [3].

## Apple Calendar

### Preset Colors

Apple Calendar offers preset colors per-calendar (not per-event) [11].
Custom colors are available via the macOS color picker [11]. Official Apple
documentation does not publish hex values for the presets [32].

### Dark Mode Behavior

Apple Calendar follows the system-wide dark mode setting — there is no
independent dark mode toggle [11]. No public documentation describes how
Apple adapts preset colors for dark backgrounds [11][32].

### Status Encoding

Apple uses symbol-based indicators rather than fill patterns for event
status [11]. Individual invitee responses are shown with distinct icons for:
accepted, maybe, declined, available/no response, unavailable/no response,
and unknown availability [11]. In month view, all-day events show as color
bars and timed events as colored dots [11].

## Microsoft Outlook

### Category Colors (25 total)

Outlook defines 25 category colors via the OlCategoryColor enum [26].
RGB/hex values for Outlook 2016 [9]:

| Category | Hex | Category | Hex |
|----------|-----|----------|-----|
| Red | #F07D88 | DarkRed | #910A19 |
| Orange | #FF8C00 | DarkOrange | #CE4B28 |
| Peach | #FECB6F | DarkPeach | #A47332 |
| Yellow | #FFF100 | DarkYellow | #B0A923 |
| Green | #5FBE7D | DarkGreen | #026802 |
| Teal | #33BAB1 | DarkTeal | #1C6367 |
| Olive | #A3B367 | DarkOlive | #5C6A22 |
| Blue | #55ABE5 | DarkBlue | #254069 |
| Purple | #A895E2 | DarkPurple | #562685 |
| Maroon | #E48BB5 | DarkMaroon | #80275D |
| Steel | #B9C0CB | Black | #474747 |
| DarkSteel | #4C596E | Gray | #ABABAB |

Outlook 365/2019 uses updated values (e.g., Red became #DC626D) [9].

### Dark Mode Adaptation

Microsoft uses a semantic color system where "a single color swatch has two or
more color values" that change between light and dark mode [22]. The approach
increases brightness while reducing saturation [22].

Users report New Outlook dark mode made colors "too muted" — yellow described as
"diaper brown," blue as muted, red as "wine color" [22]. This was flagged as an
accessibility concern by users.

Mobile Outlook uses pure black as primary surface color for OLED battery
savings, with neutral grays for cards and dialogs [22].

## Fantastical

Fantastical supports dark mode following the system theme [28]. Events inherit
calendar color by default with per-event color overrides available [12].

No specific dark-mode hex values or color adaptation methodology is publicly
documented for Fantastical [12][28].

## Cross-Application Summary

| App | # Event Colors | Dark Mode Approach | Public Dark Hex Values |
|-----|---------------|-------------------|----------------------|
| Google Calendar | 11 event + 24 calendar | Algorithmic desaturation + brightness | No |
| Apple Calendar | Presets + custom | System-wide, undocumented adaptation | No |
| Outlook | 25 categories | Semantic color mapping, brightness↑ saturation↓ | No |
| Fantastical | Calendar-inherited | System-wide, undocumented | No |

**Key finding:** No major calendar application publishes its dark-mode event
color hex values. All use some form of desaturation and brightness adjustment,
but the algorithms are proprietary. Google's is the best documented at a
principles level [3], but still lacks specific values.

## Gaps and Limitations

- No dark-mode hex values could be sourced from any vendor's public documentation
- Apple Calendar's preset color hex values could not be verified from Apple sources [32]
- Google Calendar's internal desaturation algorithm is described only at the principle level [3]
- Fantastical's dark mode color handling is effectively undocumented [12][28]
